objective: Assess commit b36e708 (ripgrep and fd run from PATH instead of bundled pinned binaries) for security vulnerabilities.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-unbundle, branch release/0.3.2/feat/user-installed-search-tools. The change is commit b36e708; review `git diff 3cc15367 b36e708` (source, tests, docs and instruction text without the generated dist: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad/unbundle-src.diff; the dist also deletes the vendored binaries and regenerates bundles and agent files). Head 86e6d051 only adds a no-content merge of the integration branch.

Requirement (maintainer, verbatim: "remove the bundling of the executables, list them as dependencies instead", then "I mean dependencies for the users"): HolyAgent stops bundling ripgrep and fd; they become prerequisites the user installs; holyagent rg and holyagent fd run the ones on PATH (fd also as Debian's fdfind); a missing tool fails with install commands per platform; setup and doctor of the Claude plugin and of Pi report them; mise provides them for development and CI; instructions tell agents to fall back to the system search tools when one is missing; docs list them as prerequisites; the updater no longer moves vendored binaries.

Read the diff file above; you have no shell. Trace: how the binary is resolved (PATH order, the current directory or a project-relative PATH entry, Windows PATHEXT and the current-directory search of Windows, a repository that ships an `rg` or `fd` or `fdfind` file), argument passing to the resolved binary (shell interpolation), what replaces the removed checksum verification, and whether the mise tool sources in mise.toml pin and verify what they download.
constraints: Work only inside /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-unbundle; never check out a branch, commit or make any git write in /home/user/holyagent or any other worktree, and make no edits.
Never start pi or make live Kimi, Codex or OpenAI requests.
Mark each finding blocking or non-blocking, with file:line and a concrete failure scenario. Report in under 450 words.

result:
result: no blocking vulnerability found in b36e708; 3 non-blocking items (2 suspicions, 1 hardening gap). Built-in `/security-review` could not run: its `git diff origin/HEAD...` failed with "unknown revision" (no origin/HEAD in this clone), so it covered nothing. I reviewed the diff file plus worktree source by reading only; no shell, nothing executed.

Findings (all non-blocking):
1. Suspicion, non-blocking: PATH resolution does not exclude cwd-relative entries, and there is no test. `findCommand` (packages/runtime/src/setup/shell.ts:50-64) calls `Bun.which(cmd, {PATH: env PATH})` with no `cwd` option and no absolute-only filter. `runTool` (packages/runtime/src/cli/tools.ts, `locateTool`/`findCommand` call at about diff line 3967) then spawns the result. Source: `env.PATH` plus the project working directory. Sink: `$\`${path} ...\``.
   - If PATH has a relative entry (`.`, `bin`) or an empty segment, a cloned repo that ships `rg` or `fdfind` runs when an agent calls `holyagent rg` or `holyagent fd`. This is a user-environment precondition; the old bundled absolute path had no such exposure.
   - On Windows, whether Bun implicitly searches the current directory, or in what order it applies PATHEXT, is unverified from here. If it does, a repo-shipped `rg.exe`/`rg.cmd` runs on first use.
   - tests/tools.test.ts covers neither case (it uses `bin` as the whole PATH).
   - Fix: filter PATH entries to `isAbsolute` before the lookup, or reject a result under `call.cwd`. Add a POSIX test with `PATH=.` and a planted `rg`. Windows needs a check on the CI `windows` job.
2. Suspicion, non-blocking: Windows `.cmd`/`.bat` shims. PATHEXT resolution can return a `rg.cmd` or `fd.cmd` shim, such as a mise or scoop shim. It would be spawned with model-controlled search arguments, so cmd.exe metacharacters could become command injection (BatBadBut class). The old bundle only ran `.exe` files. Fix: accept only `.exe` on win32, or reject `.cmd`/`.bat` results. Unverified, because Bun's behavior for batch files cannot be exercised here.
3. Hardening gap, non-blocking: mise.toml:11-12 pins `ripgrep = "15.2.0"` and `fd = "10.5.2"`, but there is no `mise.lock` and no explicit backend prefix. Integrity then depends on mise's default backend for these names, which I could not verify offline. This is the same posture as the existing `bun` pin. The checksum verification in scripts/update-dependencies.ts (the published SHA-256 and the `ChecksumMismatch` check) is deleted. `MISE_SOURCES` now moves the versions with no hash step, so after the change, mise's own verification is all that remains. CI (validation.yml `jdx/mise-action`, SHA-pinned) installs them in jobs that do not hold `contents: write`. Recommend a committed `mise.lock`, or an explicit `aqua:` backend, if checksum assurance is wanted.

Checked and sound:
- Argument passing: the Bun `$` template gets an absolute path and an array of arguments, so each is escaped as one word. The POSIX test passes `$HOME`, `a*b`, `two words`, `--help` and `--` through unchanged.
- No install command is ever executed: `installAdvice` and `INSTALL_COMMANDS` are static strings, and setup and doctor only look programs up.
- `ToolMissing` messages are static, and the env passed to the child is the same as before (`definedEnv`).
- `rg --pre` and a user `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` are unchanged from the bundled behavior.
- The change removes the archive-extraction and download code paths (`vendor.ts`, `installAsset`), which shrinks the attack surface.
- build.ts now `rm`s only `GENERATED_PATHS`, with no new path input.
- fd resolves as `fd`, then `fdfind`; `rg` only as `rg`.
